$Comment: Charge 0.8 s with ice sparks on the staff, then fire Projectile_Config_AT_Ice_King_Ray. Built like vanilla Goblin_Duke_Magic_1. 2026-10-21 (playtest: an effect on his hands whenever he casts): ice-blue hand glow AT_Ice_King_Summon_Energy on R-Hand and L-Hand during the charge. 2026-10-21 (thrown with one hand, sometimes right, sometimes left, like the burst): the charge uses FrostBeamCharging (hands beside the head) instead of CastSummon; then IceRayThrow (right) or IceRayThrowL (left, 0.5 s each) and the bolt from that hand (_R / _L projectile configs). The hands alternate through the AT_Ice_King_Ray_Hand_L flag (no random pick exists among interactions). The staff spark (Impact_Ice on Handle) stays in the charge. Only the right-hand projectile carries the AimingReference tag (one per Attack root). Built as a Serial [charge, hand pick] (2026-10-21) so no piece keeps the id of the old single projectile ('..._Next'): after hot reloads the server kept that id's AimingReference tag and refused the Attack root. 2026-10-21 (playtest: the charge matches the throwing hand): the hand is picked first, then FrostBeamCharging/IceRayThrow (right) or FrostBeamChargingL/IceRayThrowL (left). The Serial now holds only the hand pick, so no piece reuses an id that had the AimingReference tag before.

Interactions.$Comment: Which hand, decided BEFORE the charge so the wind-up matches the throw: with AT_Ice_King_Ray_Hand_L on him -> FrostBeamChargingL (left arm back), IceRayThrowL, left bolt, flag cleared; without it -> FrostBeamCharging (right arm back), IceRayThrow, right bolt, flag put on.

Next.$Comment: No AimingReference tag here: an NPC Attack root may hold only ONE (server: 'Has too many AimingReference tags', the whole air enraged component failed to load). The right-hand bolt carries it; both bolts fly the same, so his aim is the same either way.

Left hand: chained with Next (not a Serial) so these pieces get new ids; after a hot reload the server kept the AimingReference tag of the old left-bolt id and refused the Attack root ('too many AimingReference tags').
